notice: Torque values come from three tiers, each marked: Triumph documents (owner handbook, Technical News bulletin), the aftermarket Haynes manual, and owner forum posts. No Triumph service manual for these models was available to this project; where only Haynes gives a value, treat it as aftermarket.

specs.name: Engine oil grade
specs.value: Semi or fully synthetic 10W/40 or 10W/50, API SH or higher and JASO MA

specs.name: Oil filter
specs.value: 10 Nm, Triumph tool T3880313 to remove

specs.name: Factory chain
specs.value: DID 525 VM2 or DID 520 VM2, 104 links

rows.task: Engine and oil cooler - check for leaks
Autoscan - carry out a full Autoscan using the Triumph diagnostic tool
Fuel system - check for leaks, chafing etc.
Lights, instruments and electrical systems - check
Brake master cylinders - check for fluid leaks
Brake calipers - check for fluid leaks and seized pistons
Spokes (where fitted) - check for broken or damaged spokes, check spoke tightness
Wheel bearings - check for wear/smooth operation

notes: Whichever comes first, distance or time. Brake fluid is renewed every 2 years; the chain is lubricated every 300 km and wear-checked every 800 km.
Evaporative hoses are fitted only for certain markets.
Source: Triumph owner's handbook 3851861-IN, January 2015, pages 63–64. Triumph advises that an authorised dealer carries out scheduled maintenance.

right.subject: Triumph Bonneville T100, 2011 model year
right.relevance: A 2011 T100, three years before the A3 range. It has the same 865 cc twin, spoked wheels and chrome engine covers. No openly licensed 2014–2016 T100 side view was found. A flyscreen and rack are fitted. It is not the owner's motorcycle.
